Full write up below. I hope the data in the report is useful to reporters, researchers, policymakers, elected leaders, and the broad public. Feel free to use any of these tables and graphs with attribution. 

austinkocher.substack.com/p/…
And where were most people in DH originally arrested? Mostly in NJ and NY, although some were transferred from outside the region.

Can ICE deport people in DH? Mostly no. As of mid-March, the majority of people held at Delaney Hall—84.2%—did not have a final removal order. In the past, the gov often chose not to waste taxpayer $$$ detaining people it can't deport and don't represent a threat to pub safety.

What about all 10,311 people to pass through DH since May 2025? Just two (0.02%) had homicide conviction (0.07% if you incl all manslaughter), 24 (0.2%) sex. assault conviction, 19 (0.2%) drug traffic, 9 (0.09%) robbery, 12 (0.1%) agg assault.

Is DH holding "murderers, rapists, pedophiles and drug traffickers"? ICE's data says vast majority have no conviction (88.3%) + large majority have no crim history (70.5%). If you were looking for an ICE facility that holds a large number of dangerous criminals, DH isn't it.

In a PR on May 25, ICE pushed back on criticisms of DH: “These sanctuary politicians should be thanking ICE for removing murderers, rapists, pedophiles, and drug traffickers from their communities. We need politicians cooperate with us to get criminals out of their state.”
Once DH opened last year, it QUICKLY became the main detention site in the great NYC-Newark area, much larger than Elizabeth or Brooklyn MDC. A LOT of people are held or pass through this facility.

How many people are held there? Detention Reports finds ~850 people as of early April, but ICE refuses to release more data. This makes DH the largest ICE facility in the Northeast and the East Coast. 

detentionreports.com/facilit…

Since DH reopened, ICE + GEO Group refused to allow inspections of the facility to ensure compliance with local/state law and blocked elected leaders from access. People inside report food w/ maggots, poor medical care, unsanitary facilities. Jean Wilson Brutus died there in Dec.

Background: Delaney Hall was used for imm detention 2011-2017, closed, then reopened in May 2025 under Trump II. BUT! -> Contracting started in the summer of 2024 under Biden. This is a Biden/Trump facility.

ICE insists that it needs to spend $1B detaining people inside Delaney Hall to protect Americans from "murderers, rapists, and pedophiles." People inside and protestors outside say the facility is inhumane, exploitive, and unnecessary. What does the data say? 🧵

Full breakdown of: who's inside, where they were arrested, how Delaney Hall fits into ICE's northeast network is here: 
austinkocher.substack.com/p/…
One caveat: the most recent data is from March. ICE hasn't released updates since. A lot can change in two months inside a detention facility, so note that if you're citing these numbers.
This is a $1 billion, 15-year facility run by GEO Group. 84% of people inside as of March didn't even have a final removal order, meaning ICE couldn't deport them. Not yet anyway.

I also looked at everyone who has passed through Delaney Hall since it reopened (all 10,311 people): 
Homicide convictions: 0.02%
Sexual assault: 0.2%
Drug trafficking: 0.2%

ICE's story fits less than 1% of the people ever held there.

Of the 99 people with convictions in the facility as of March, the most common offenses were DUIs, illegal entry, larceny, and shoplifting. Not one conviction for homicide, sexual assault, or drug trafficking.
70.5% of people held there have no criminal history at all. Another 17.8% have charges only, no conviction. Just 11.7% have any conviction on record.

ICE says it needs Delaney Hall to lock up "murderers, rapists, and pedophiles."
I looked at the data. That's not who's inside.

ICE insists that it needs to spend $1 billion dollars detaining people inside Delaney Hall to protect Americans from "murderers, rapists, and pedophiles." The data tell a different story.
